name: Bramah hydraulic press at the Tower of London
description: A Bramah hydraulic pressing machine was in use at the Tower of London in 1806.

impact.note: One press in use at one site, witnessing a fairly new machine; nothing later is known to rest on this installation.

date.basis: The date applies to this documented case, not to the worldwide origin of the capability.

events.statement: The museum reports Bramah’s hydraulic press patent in 1795 and use of the preserved press at the Tower of London in 1806.

evidence.supports: The museum reports Bramah’s hydraulic press patent in 1795 and use of the preserved press at the Tower of London in 1806.

earliest_record.rationale: Earliest researched operational or depicted case for this record, not a claim of global priority.

caveats: The museum does not identify the press’s precise 1806 task, throughput or customer terms.

research.note: Independent review checked the Sheffield museum account identifying the specific preserved press in service at the Tower in 1806, distinct from the 1795 patent.
